kept.heading: OPENAI IS BACKING AWAY FROM REDDIT AS REDDIT TRIES TO BECOME OPENAI? (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reddit's citations in ChatGPT have fallen from as high as 4.5% of responses to about 0.5% after OpenAI changed how it searches the web. Reddit says it still gets most of its traffic from direct visits and traditional search. Meanwhile, Reddit is using AI to turn posts and comments into videos and podcasts, with the company aiming to make its content easier to consume in the background.

kept.heading: HOW GEN ALPHA IS REDEFINING BACK-TO-SCHOOL SPENDING (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Gen Alpha is gaining more influence over household spending. 48% of parental spending in the US and UK is directly influenced by kids. Back-to-school shoppers plan to spend $922 on average, while 73% of families expect to use AI to research products, compare prices, or plan budgets. Kids are also gaining more control over purchases, with 40% of parents allowing them to add items directly to digital carts.

kept.heading: HOW TO TELL IF YOUR PERSONALIZATION IS OVER THE LINE (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Personalization crosses the line when a company reacts more aggressively than a customer's actual behavior justifies. One browsing session for a single product followed the author across Instagram, other sites' ad inventory, and their inbox within hours. That reach is exactly what over-personalization feels like from the customer's side. The fix is to run every tactic through three tests: would a customer expect it, does the data meaningfully improve their experience, and is the value worth how sensitive it feels? A purchase or an explicit preference justifies a stronger response than a few seconds of browsing ever should.

kept.heading: THE CONDITIONAL-PROMOTION PARADOX: HOW CONDITIONAL DISCOUNTS HURT TOTAL SALES (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A discount that only kicks in after a big commitment can backfire and shrink total sales instead of growing them. A $700 discount on a $1,000 phone that only applies if the buyer signs a new two-year service contract is attractive, but the requirement is very high. Many shoppers can't take it. Seeing the discount at all makes paying full price feel like a worse deal than before. Instead of buying anyway, they walk away completely. The fix is to keep the requirement small, or target the offer only at customers who can easily meet it. A low-cost requirement paired with a big discount actually increases total sales the most.

kept.heading: AI FORCED WASHINGTON POST TO RETHINK PAID ACQUISITION, START WITH JOURNALISM (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI search is shrinking the organic funnel, so publishers need paid media to create demand rather than simply convert existing intent. The Washington Post found journalist-led video delivered more than 4x the CTR of traditional direct response creative, and earlier article promotion produced a 31% conversion lift over organic alone. The strategy is to turn credible, platform-native journalism into paid creative for cold and warm audiences instead of leading with subscription offers. This approach also makes better use of existing content assets while giving audiences a human credibility signal as AI-generated content becomes more common.

kept.heading: META HIGHLIGHTS RISING BRAND OPPORTUNITIES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Women's sports is becoming a major opportunity for brands, with the industry growing 4.5X faster than men's sports. Women's sports content generated 1.2B+ WNBA views and 900M women's soccer views on Meta last quarter. Athlete partnerships are especially valuable, with 76% of sports fans saying athlete content influences what they buy. Meta says brands can get ahead by partnering with women athletes while the category is still taking shape.

kept.heading: SIMILARWEB CAN NOW TRACK ADS INSIDE CHATGPT AND GOOGLE AI MODE (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The data covers competitor brands, ad creatives, messaging, landing pages, and share of voice, built from real anonymized user activity instead of synthetic prompts.

kept.heading: SAN FRANCISCO BAY AREA DETHRONED AS LARGEST ‘TECH TALENT' MARKET (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: New York's tech workforce hit 394k last year against the Bay Area's 376k, a reversal built on a 6% Bay Area decline since 2022 versus 8% growth in New York.

kept.heading: AMERICA'S MEETUP EXPLOSION (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Young people are trading apps and screens for in-person social experiences. “Soft socializing” events built around activities like trivia, mahjong, birdwatching, puzzles, and crafts are surging. Puzzle events rose 151% year over year, while mahjong events rose 94%. The trend also extends to dating, with people turning to activity-based meetups and dinner parties to find both romantic and platonic connections.

kept.heading: CREATOR FIT BEATS FOLLOWER COUNT FOR BRANDS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The creator economy is projected to reach nearly $500B by 2027, but brand partnerships are shifting from reach to fit. Suitability is now the top factor brands consider when choosing creators, while follower count ranks eighth. Yet 67% of creators earn under $10K annually, and 53% say less than 25% of their income comes from brand partnerships. Audience-brand tension is also growing, with 42% of creators reporting it overall and 53% among creators with 500K+ followers.

kept.heading: MICRO DRAMA: THE NEW CONTENT FORMAT MARKETERS CAN'T IGNORE (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A micro drama is a serialized vertical video story split into 1-3 minute episodes, each ending on a cliffhanger that pulls viewers into the next. The format is cheaper and faster to produce than traditional TV, letting creators test hooks in real time and cut anything that fails to hold attention. After years of brands chasing shorter cuts and faster hooks, micro dramas reverse the model by asking audiences to commit across multiple episodes.

kept.heading: TURN YOUR SALES CALLS INTO NEWSLETTERS WITH CLAUDE CODE (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: Your best newsletter material is already sitting in the calls you take every week. In this free webinar, Will Leatherman will walk through his Claude Code system to mine sales calls and write newsletters in your voice. It takes place on August 25 at 9 AM PT.

kept.heading: YOUTUBE IS PAYING CREATORS MILLIONS TO STAY EXCLUSIVE - AND PUNISHING THOSE WHO DON'T (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: YouTube is reportedly offering top creators millions in financing and brand revenue to stay exclusive. Creators who partner with Netflix could lose YouTube marketing support, events, and brand deals. The move shows how platforms are competing for creator exclusivity. It could also fragment creator content across platforms and force audiences to follow creators across multiple services.

kept.heading: EVERYONE KNOWS YOU. DO THEY CARE? (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands can be widely known without being relevant to the audiences they want to reach. This piece introduces an audience mapping approach that analyzes who people follow and how those interests overlap, revealing the cultural spaces a brand occupies, or misses. The goal isn't to be everywhere, but to find the communities and cultural worlds where the brand can meaningfully belong. Brands can then build a more distinctive position instead of pursuing broad appeal that resonates with no one.

kept.heading: BRAND CONFESSIONAL: DENNIS WANG (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Dennis Wang, lululemon's former VP of Accessories Design, built its accessories business from scratch to over $1B. His CPR framework treats hit products as engineered outcomes, starting with a clear Customer, solving a real friction with the Product, and building Relevancy into the experience. He favors community and partnerships over transactional influencer campaigns.

kept.heading: HOW WE BUILT A RECOGNIZABLE, SCALABLE BRAND IN BROOKLYN'S CROWDED FOOD SCENE (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Lucky Parlor's branding team started with strategy, not aesthetics. They defined the brand's positioning before designing anything. The identity then centered on distinctive memory hooks, including a gyoza mark, custom lettering, colors, and illustrations. The flexible system helped the brand stay recognizable across different touchpoints as it scaled.

kept.heading: BRAND HYPE HAS EXISTED SINCE THE BRONZE AGE, SCIENTISTS DISCOVER (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A 3,200-year-old pottery tradition may be one of the earliest examples of branding.

kept.heading: HERE'S HOW TO BUILD YOUR MARKETING TEAM FOR THE AI ERA (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Marketing roles are shifting toward AI-fluent generalists as job postings fall and AI mentions nearly double to 15%.

kept.heading: HOW TO MEASURE THE TRUE VALUE OF CREATORS AND REVIEW CONTENT (8 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Measure review content by incremental impact, not attributed affiliate revenue.
